name: Hardware drivers (DriverKit and USB)
plain: Runs user space drivers for hardware; on iPadOS only on M series iPads.
meaning: Lets apps talk to USB and PCIe style accessories; power and risk justify Apple approval and user approval.

android.permission: None; per device USB permission dialog
android.note: No kernel or arbitrary drivers for apps

ios.prompt_ui: User enables the driver in Settings
ios.revocation: Settings > General > Login Items and Extensions > Drivers
ios.note: iPadOS 16 and later on M1 and newer iPads; macOS uses same API

limits.headline: Can run hardware drivers only on M series iPads, with Apple approval
limits.user_action: You turn the driver on in Settings, then plug in the device
can: Run a driver for a USB or similar accessory on iPad with M1 or newer (iPadOS 16 and later)
Talk to a USB device on Android after you tap Allow
cannot: Run a driver on iPad without Apple's entitlement and your switch in Settings
Install kernel or arbitrary drivers on Android
limits.reach_label: Devices you plug in and approve
limits.differs: iPad needs Apple's approval and your switch in Settings; Android only offers a per device USB prompt.

story.what_it_is: Lets a company run its own device driver as a normal app, instead of changing the system.

marketing.name: DriverKit
marketing.pitch: Build drivers for USB and PCIe style gear that run as apps and need no system changes.

story.for_you: You plug in a pro audio box or lab device on an iPad Pro and it just works after you install the maker's app. You do not see the driver, only the device working.
story.for_makers: Hardware makers can support the iPad without a system change. Apple approves each use. This opens the iPad to music studios, labs and scientists. Android does not let apps act as drivers.

use_cases.example: A pro audio interface works with iPad music apps after you install its driver app.
A classroom science kit plugs into an iPad to record data.
A tablet runs a barcode scanner and printer for a store.
An engineer tests hardware from an iPad.
A lab device streams results to a clinician's iPad.
A video capture card feeds a live editor.
A hardware key reader unlocks a company app.

story.android_note: Android does not allow apps to act as drivers for arbitrary hardware.
story.ios_note: On iPadOS this only works on iPads with M1 or newer chips. macOS uses the same API.

technical_bounds: Android lacks driver model but offers USB host
